'''''Cistus albidus''''', the '''grey-leaved cistus''',<ref name=BSBI07/> is a [[shrub]]by [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Cistaceae]], with pink to purple flowers, native to south-western Europe and western north Africa.

==Description==
''Cistus albidus'' grows up to {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on|0}} tall. Its leaves are oblong to elliptical in shape, usually {{convert|2|–|5|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} long by {{convert|0.5|–|2|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} wide. They have three prominent veins and are densely covered with short hairs, producing a greyish-white appearance. The flowers are arranged in [[cyme (botany)|cyme]]s of one to seven individual flowers, each {{convert|4|–|6|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} across with five purple to pink [[petal]]s and five [[sepal]]s.<ref name=Warb68/>

==Taxonomy and phylogeny ==
''Cistus albidus'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753 in ''[[Species Plantarum]]'' (p. 524).<ref name=TPL_kew-2723264/> The specific epithet ''albidus'' means "whitish", referring to the leaves and shoots.<ref name=Coom94p42/>

A 2011 [[Molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic study]] placed ''C. albidus'' as the sister to ''[[Cistus creticus]]'' in the purple and pink flowered clade (PPC) of ''Cistus'' species. ''C. creticus'' is found largely in the eastern Mediterranean, and the distributions of the two species show little overlap. They are able to hybridize, producing the fertile hybrid ''C.'' × ''canescens''.<ref name=CiveLeclDemoAgna11/>

The [[sister group]] to both species is ''[[Cistus heterophyllus|C. heterophyllus]]''.

==Distribution==
''Cistus albidus'' is native to the west of [[Southern Europe]] and western [[North Africa]], particularly around the [[Mediterranean]], including [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], the [[Balearic Islands]], [[France]], [[Corsica]], [[Italy]], [[Sardinia]],<ref name=Warb68/> and [[Morocco]].<ref name=CiveLeclDemoAgna11/>
